criteria.title: Explicit research question
criteria.description: Whether the question, target object or population, and conditions identify what would answer the study.

anchors.0: No recoverable question, or incompatible tasks make the intended answer indeterminate.
anchors.1: A topic is named, but the target, comparison or success condition needed to identify an answer is missing.
anchors.2: The central question is identifiable; a consequential population, regime or outcome boundary remains ambiguous.
anchors.3: Question, target and answer conditions are explicit; a secondary boundary needs clarification.
anchors.4: A precise question and its conditions distinguish the intended answer from adjacent questions throughout the inspected account.

checks: Restate the question from manuscript passages; identify its target and answer condition.
Compare the stated task with actual outputs, endpoints or theorem targets.
Identify what observation or argument could answer this question rather than a nearby one.

criteria.title: Motivation and evidenced gap
criteria.description: Whether a specific unresolved need follows from prior knowledge and has an explained consequence for the intended reader.

anchors.0: No reason for the study is supplied, or the stated gap contradicts the inspected account.
anchors.1: Broad importance or an unsupported absence claim substitutes for a specific unresolved need.
anchors.2: A plausible gap is identified, but its evidence or intellectual or practical consequence is weakly explained.
anchors.3: Specific prior limitations support the need and its consequence; a bounded premise remains underexplained.
anchors.4: Inspected prior knowledge, the unresolved need and its consequence form a traceable rationale without manufacturing a universal gap.

checks: Locate the gap statement and the source or observation supporting each premise.
Explain what remains unresolved after the closest prior work and why it matters.
Replace unsupported first, none or all claims with evidenced scope.

criteria.title: Contribution and value calibration
criteria.description: Whether the declared contribution type, distinction from prior work, and value match what the work adds.

anchors.0: No addition is identifiable, or the declared contribution contradicts the work described.
anchors.1: Novelty or superiority slogans obscure what changed and what value the change provides.
anchors.2: A concrete addition is named, but its novelty, usefulness or contribution type is overstated or conflated.
anchors.3: Contribution type, concrete addition and value are bounded and credible; a secondary distinction needs sharpening.
anchors.4: Each addition has a specific distinction and justified value appropriate to its type, including replication, resource, negative or theoretical contributions.

checks: State the contribution type and what the reader gains beyond the closest alternative.
Separate newness, usefulness and measured superiority.
Compare contribution bullets with delivered objects, analyses or propositions.

criteria.title: Literature positioning and attribution
criteria.description: Whether relevant alternatives and source passages are represented accurately enough to locate the contribution and credit prior work.

anchors.0: Central cited support is nonexistent or demonstrably misrepresented, or no prior-work context is given.
anchors.1: Citation lists or selective caricatures omit directly relevant alternatives and make central attribution unreliable.
anchors.2: Relevant work is discussed, but an important distinction, contrary result or cited clause remains unsupported.
anchors.3: Closest alternatives and contrary evidence are accurately distinguished using inspected passages; bounded source gaps are disclosed.
anchors.4: Traceable attribution explains relevant alternatives, preserves contradictory evidence and supports central literature-dependent distinctions in the inspected scope.

checks: Inspect source passages for central cited clauses; record versions and locations.
Compare settings, assumptions and contributions with the closest alternatives rather than counting citations.
Mark inaccessible sources unverified; a citation identifier does not verify support.

criteria.title: Method and procedure specification
criteria.description: Whether procedures, constructions and choices are reported well enough to understand what was done.

anchors.0: The central procedure or construction is absent or impossible to identify.
anchors.1: A method label or sketch omits decisive steps, inputs or selection choices.
anchors.2: The main procedure is recoverable, but a consequential implementation, derivation or analysis choice is underspecified.
anchors.3: Inputs, steps, choices and outputs are specified; remaining omissions affect secondary details.
anchors.4: The procedure can be reconstructed from explicit inputs, transformations, selection rules and outputs, with departures from cited methods identified.

checks: Trace an input through decisive processing or reasoning steps to the output.
Record relevant data or object versions, selection rules and parameters.
Distinguish a specified procedure from an assertion that a standard method was used.

criteria.title: Design and inferential validity
criteria.description: Whether the inspected design or formal argument can support the intended inference under stated assumptions.

anchors.0: An inspected fatal design error, invalid proof step or incompatible assumption defeats the central inference.
anchors.1: Major threats such as leakage, inappropriate units, missing identification assumptions or a proof gap remain unresolved.
anchors.2: The design or argument addresses the question, but a consequential validity threat is only partly handled.
anchors.3: Design choices and assumptions support the intended inference; a bounded threat remains with its consequence stated.
anchors.4: Relevant sampling, identification or proof obligations are inspected and addressed for the stated inference, with explicit conditions and no unresolved material threat in that scope.

checks: Identify the estimand or formal target and the assumptions connecting evidence to it.
Inspect development/evaluation separation, independence or proof dependencies as applicable.
Distinguish an observed invalid step from an uninspected step; use unassessed when validity cannot yet be judged.

criteria.title: Comparisons and alternative explanations
criteria.description: Whether comparisons are interpretable under matched or explicitly different conditions and address the attributed cause of an effect.

anchors.0: A central superiority or attribution claim relies on a known incompatible comparison presented as equivalent.
anchors.1: Relevant alternatives or decisive condition differences are omitted, leaving the central comparison confounded.
anchors.2: Useful comparisons exist, but a material resource, assumption or selection mismatch limits interpretation.
anchors.3: Relevant alternatives and comparison conditions are reported; remaining differences constrain only a bounded claim.
anchors.4: Comparisons answer their stated question with matched conditions or explicit differences; necessary controls distinguish central attribution from plausible alternatives.

checks: List comparator eligibility, assumptions, inputs, resources and selection access on both sides.
Separate reproduced results from values copied from publications.
For component claims, check what else changed; otherwise limit the claim to the observed system contrast.

criteria.title: Analysis and uncertainty interpretation
criteria.description: Whether analyses, variability or formal bounds are defined and interpreted with the assumptions and precision the claim requires.

anchors.0: The central analysis is absent or demonstrably misinterpreted, such as treating nonsignificance as established equivalence.
anchors.1: Central estimates or bounds lack essential calculation, dependence, interval or probability meaning.
anchors.2: The main estimate or bound is interpretable, but an important uncertainty source, analysis choice or condition remains unclear.
anchors.3: Analysis choices, precision and represented uncertainty are explained; a bounded unrepresented source is acknowledged.
anchors.4: Estimates or guarantees have traceable calculations, appropriate units or quantifiers, and calibrated interpretation of relevant uncertainty, assumptions and analysis selection.

checks: Identify analysis target, independent unit and represented randomness, or theorem quantifiers and regime.
Distinguish SD, SE, confidence, credible and prediction intervals; inspect evaluation of the contrast itself.
Check effect magnitude and analysis selection rather than imposing a p-value threshold or fixed seed quota.

criteria.title: Robustness, sensitivity and failures
criteria.description: Whether evidence probes consequential sensitivities and failure conditions relevant to the contribution.

anchors.0: Known central failures are suppressed or contradicted, or an unrestricted robustness claim has no supporting examination.
anchors.1: Consequential sensitivities or counterexamples are ignored despite reliance on broad stability claims.
anchors.2: Some sensitivity or failure evidence is supplied, but a central fragile condition remains unexplored or unexplained.
anchors.3: Principal sensitivities and observed failures are examined; remaining probes are bounded by the stated scope.
anchors.4: Claim-relevant stress tests, sensitivity arguments or counterexamples locate where conclusions persist or fail, preserving adverse findings and unresolved conditions.

checks: Choose sensitivity checks that could change a central conclusion and explain their relevance.
Separate observed failure, inconclusive result, unmeasured condition and unavailable evidence.
Inspect whether exceptions change the conclusion or require a narrower regime.

criteria.title: Claim-to-evidence entailment
criteria.description: Whether each central statement follows from its inspected evidence at the stated strength and scope.

anchors.0: A central claim contradicts its cited result or asserts an inference the inspected evidence cannot support.
anchors.1: Central claims lack support or exceed the evidence's population, comparator, causal status or formal conditions.
anchors.2: Most central claims map to evidence, but a consequential scope or inference mismatch remains.
anchors.3: Central claims follow from identified results or arguments; a secondary qualification or evidence link needs repair.
anchors.4: Every inspected central claim links to supporting results or arguments and preserves their comparator, conditions, uncertainty and inferential strength.

checks: Map exact headline and conclusion clauses to table cells, analyses, proof steps or source passages.
Check observation versus mechanism, association versus causation, and prediction versus demonstrated utility.
Propose specific missing evidence or a claim revision that existing evidence supports.

criteria.title: Concept definitions and identity
criteria.description: Whether central constructs have operational meanings and retain their identity across terms and sections.

anchors.0: A central concept has incompatible meanings or no recoverable definition.
anchors.1: Undefined or overloaded constructs obscure what is manipulated, measured or proved.
anchors.2: Central constructs are mostly defined, but a consequential alias or boundary remains ambiguous.
anchors.3: Definitions and permitted aliases preserve central identities; a secondary term needs disambiguation.
anchors.4: Operational definitions distinguish central constructs, and tracing sections shows stable meanings and explicit relationships among aliases.

checks: Build a concept ledger with definition, canonical label, permitted aliases and first definition.
Inspect efficiency, generalization, clinical utility and other overloaded words against the quantity studied.
Cite conflicting passages; do not treat harmless grammatical variation as changed meaning.

criteria.title: Notation, units and formal references
criteria.description: Whether symbols, dimensions, units and formal labels are defined and used consistently.

anchors.0: A central equation or quantity has contradictory symbols or dimensions that prevent interpretation.
anchors.1: Repeated undefined or changing symbols, scales or units obscure central calculations.
anchors.2: Main notation and units are recoverable, but a consequential collision, conversion or reference remains unresolved.
anchors.3: Central symbols, domains, scales and units are consistent; bounded secondary definitions need repair.
anchors.4: Symbols and domains are defined before dependency, units and conversions are coherent, and equation, theorem and panel references resolve in the inspected material.

checks: Trace central symbols to definitions, domains, shapes or dimensions as relevant.
Check conversions, scale factors and metric direction across equations, text and displays.
Resolve symbol collisions and broken formal references without changing mathematical meaning.

criteria.title: Numbers, denominators and aggregation
criteria.description: Whether quantities agree, identify what is counted, and use correct denominators, aggregation and change descriptions.

anchors.0: A central numeric statement contradicts the supplied result or uses a denominator that reverses its meaning.
anchors.1: Central counts, percentages or summaries cannot reconcile because denominators or aggregation are missing or inconsistent.
anchors.2: Principal quantities are traceable, but a consequential count, rounding, aggregation or relative-change ambiguity remains.
anchors.3: Central numbers and denominators reconcile across inspected locations; a bounded secondary discrepancy remains.
anchors.4: Counts, exclusions, counting units, aggregation and numeric changes reconcile to identified results, distinguishing relative change from percentage points where relevant.

checks: Identify the counting unit, denominator, exclusions and aggregation for central n values, percentages and summaries.
Recompute differences and relative changes from supplied values, preserving rounding and metric direction.
In numeric-free theory inspect constants, dimensions, complexity orders and quantified counts; do not invent empirical counts.

criteria.title: Alignment across manuscript components
criteria.description: Whether repeated facts and claims agree across title, abstract, body, displays and supplement.

anchors.0: Components make incompatible central claims or report different central facts without explanation.
anchors.1: Material differences in endpoint, population, comparator, result or conditions persist between summary and body.
anchors.2: The main account agrees, but an important qualification or version change is not propagated to dependent locations.
anchors.3: Central facts, conditions and conclusions align; a bounded secondary inconsistency remains.
anchors.4: Tracing summaries, methods, results, captions, discussion and supplied supplement reconciles repeated central facts, labels and qualifications.

checks: Compare a claim ledger with title, abstract, introduction, results, captions and conclusion.
Trace revised definitions, dataset versions, endpoints and qualifiers to dependent passages.
Distinguish appropriate summary omissions from contradictions or lost decisive conditions.

criteria.title: Title and abstract communication
criteria.description: Whether summaries orient readers to the question, approach, principal result and essential boundary in the available format.

anchors.0: The title or abstract is missing or does not identify the subject and principal message.
anchors.1: Vague slogans or method names replace the question, approach or interpretable principal finding.
anchors.2: The study is identifiable, but a main result, comparison or essential boundary is difficult to recover.
anchors.3: Question, approach and bounded principal finding are clear; a secondary qualifier or structural detail needs improvement.
anchors.4: Within the applicable format, title and abstract efficiently convey the study and an interpretable principal finding with the conditions needed to read it correctly.

checks: Recover what was asked, done and found from title and abstract alone.
Retain the comparator, scale and decisive qualifier needed to interpret the headline result.
Check structured headings for the actual journal and design rather than imposing one template.

criteria.title: Introduction argument sequence
criteria.description: Whether the introduction leads from reader context through the unresolved problem to this question and contribution.

anchors.0: No argument connecting context, problem and study is recoverable from the introduction.
anchors.1: Disconnected background or citation lists force the reader to invent the connection to this study.
anchors.2: The main progression is visible, but a consequential logical bridge or study rationale is buried or missing.
anchors.3: Context, unresolved problem, question and contribution form a clear progression with a bounded transition gap.
anchors.4: Each stage supplies context needed for the next, making why this question and approach follow readily recoverable without unnecessary background.

checks: State each argumentative step and locate its bridge to the next.
Check that background serves the question and contributions follow the stated problem.
Respect genre conventions instead of forcing results or one fixed outline into every introduction.

criteria.title: Paragraph and sentence logic
criteria.description: Whether local prose makes actors, dependencies, referents and reasoning accessible without changing scientific meaning.

anchors.0: Central passages are uninterpretable because sentence relations or referents cannot be recovered.
anchors.1: Repeated missing links, ambiguous referents or noun stacks obscure the central reasoning.
anchors.2: The argument is recoverable with effort, but consequential local ambiguities or misplaced qualifications remain.
anchors.3: Paragraph purposes and sentence dependencies are clear; local friction affects secondary passages.
anchors.4: Inspected prose connects context, reasoning and takeaway with explicit referents and preserved conditions, so readers need not supply missing links.

checks: State each consequential paragraph's job and locate its evidence-to-takeaway link.
Resolve ambiguous referents and buried actors; check whether therefore and because express supported links.
Preserve negation, causal status, numbers and qualifiers when editing; use no sentence-length or voice quota.

criteria.title: Jargon, acronyms and audience access
criteria.description: Whether necessary technical language is introduced where and at the level the declared audience needs.

anchors.0: Unexplained central terminology or abbreviations prevent the intended reader from identifying the method or finding.
anchors.1: Repeated undefined jargon or competing abbreviations require substantial outside inference.
anchors.2: Most terms are usable, but a consequential first-use definition, expansion or audience explanation is missing.
anchors.3: Necessary terms and acronyms are introduced in their reading scopes; a bounded secondary access problem remains.
anchors.4: Technical distinctions are preserved with concise first-use explanations, useful abbreviations and independently readable components suited to the audience.

checks: Check unfamiliar terms at first use in abstract and body independently and in separately read displays as required.
Explain necessary distinctions with definitions or examples rather than deleting them.
Remove ornamental jargon or low-value new acronyms; document venue-specific exceptions.

criteria.title: Blind reader teach-back
criteria.description: Whether an intended reader, before seeing the author's explanation, recovers the question, approach, evidence and scope from the reading packet.

anchors.0: A saved blind reading recovers a materially contrary central question, finding or scope because of the supplied wording.
anchors.1: The blind reader cannot recover several central elements or supplies unsupported links from outside the packet.
anchors.2: The reader recovers the principal message but misses a consequential mechanism, evidence link or boundary.
anchors.3: The reader recovers question, approach, evidence and scope with passage support; a bounded secondary mismatch remains.
anchors.4: A saved blind teach-back reconstructs all packet-appropriate central elements and decisive qualifiers, with no consequential mismatch after comparison with the intended account.

checks: Save the first reader response before revealing the intended thesis or other reviews.
Require passage or display locations for recovered elements and explicit not-recoverable statements for gaps.
If no blind response exists, mark unassessed rather than inferring comprehension from polished prose.

criteria.title: Figures, tables and captions
criteria.description: Whether accessible displays convey comparisons or reasoning with interpretable labels, scales, units and captions. N/A requires absent displays and no claim needing one; document both.

anchors.0: An inspected display materially misrepresents a central result or cannot be interpreted from its labels and caption.
anchors.1: Central displays omit necessary labels, scales, units or uncertainty meaning, or obscure the intended comparison.
anchors.2: Displays convey the main message, but an important panel, scale, sampling-unit or caption ambiguity remains.
anchors.3: Accessible displays and captions make central comparisons interpretable; a bounded layout or labeling issue remains.
anchors.4: Visually inspected displays answer clear questions with legible encodings, explicit units and relevant uncertainty, and self-contained captions identifying conditions and samples.

checks: Inspect actual images and tables for legibility, axes, panels and encodings; declare caption-only limits.
Verify caption definitions of n, uncertainty, acronyms and conditions against the display.
For N/A document absent displays and why no claim needs one; inaccessible existing displays are unassessed.

criteria.title: Reproducibility route and artifacts
criteria.description: Whether readers can locate materials, derivations and provenance needed to trace or reconstruct central results under stated access conditions.

anchors.0: No route to a central result's derivation or materials is supplied, or stated artifacts are demonstrably unrelated.
anchors.1: Generic availability claims omit essential locators, versions, configurations or access procedures.
anchors.2: A usable route exists for some central results, but an important version, dependency or access restriction is unresolved.
anchors.3: Central results link to identified materials and reconstruction instructions; a bounded dependency or access detail remains.
anchors.4: A traceable route connects central results to versioned derivations or materials, configurations and access instructions, stating restrictions and the extent of actual execution or checking.

checks: Trace central results to proof locations or data, split, configuration and result files as appropriate.
Inspect artifact identity, version and access conditions; a repository URL does not establish reproduction.
Record what was rerun or checked; allow a justified alternative to public release.

criteria.title: Limitations and transfer conditions
criteria.description: Whether material limits are disclosed with their consequences for interpretation and transfer beyond studied conditions.

anchors.0: Known material limits are denied, or conclusions explicitly extend to settings excluded by the stated evidence.
anchors.1: Generic caveats avoid the design or assumption limits determining what cannot be concluded.
anchors.2: Relevant limits are named, but their effects on interpretation or transfer are incompletely explained.
anchors.3: Material limits connect to affected conclusions and plausible transfer conditions; a bounded consequence remains unclear.
anchors.4: The account explains how design, assumptions, adverse evidence and untested settings bound conclusions, preserving these conditions when discussing transfer.

checks: Connect each material limit to the claim or setting it restricts.
Separate untested transfer from observed failure and aspirations from demonstrated performance.
Check whether discussion and conclusion preserve the limits rather than ending with an unrestricted claim.

criteria.title: Ethics and truthful disclosures
criteria.description: Whether context-relevant ethics, consent, interests, funding, contributions and assistance statements are truthful and supported by supplied records.

anchors.0: A material declaration is demonstrably false or contradicts the supplied ethics, consent or contribution record.
anchors.1: Material applicable declarations or provenance are missing, or unsupported exemptions substitute for records.
anchors.2: Relevant declarations are present, but a consequential record, scope or assistance detail remains unresolved.
anchors.3: Applicable declarations agree with inspected records; a bounded secondary disclosure needs clarification.
anchors.4: Context-relevant ethical considerations and declarations are truthfully stated with record support, including explicit justified absence where an activity or requirement does not apply.

checks: Identify actual participants, data rights, sensitive uses and relevant harms before selecting checks.
Compare ethics, consent or exemption wording, funding, interests and contributions with supplied records.
Describe actual assistance under applicable policy; absent records mean unresolved, not no conflict or exempt.

criteria.title: Venue, stage and reporting requirements
criteria.description: Whether the inspected artifact meets official requirements for the declared venue, year, track, stage and study design.

anchors.0: An inspected mandatory eligibility, format or submission condition is violated in a way that prevents the intended submission.
anchors.1: Several mandatory applicable items are missing, or the wrong cycle, venue, stage or study guideline is used.
anchors.2: Applicable requirements are identified, but a consequential format, reporting or declaration item remains unresolved.
anchors.3: Mandatory requirements are checked against current official sources; a bounded nonfatal item remains to repair.
anchors.4: A dated requirement record links applicable mandatory checks to official sources and artifact locations, separating required items, recommendations and justified exclusions.

checks: Record exact venue, cycle, track, stage, official URL and access date before judging compliance.
Inspect the rendered artifact for applicable template, length, anonymity and supplement rules.
Select reporting guidance by actual design; distinguish formal compliance from scientific correctness.

empirical-ml.title: Empirical machine learning and computer vision

guidance.research-question: Name task, input access, output and evaluation setting; define the question beyond a leaderboard score.
guidance.motivation-gap: Explain the measured or conceptual need left by relevant methods; benchmark convenience alone does not establish importance.
guidance.contribution-calibration: Recognize methods, resources, analyses, replications, feasibility and negative results; SOTA is not universally required.
guidance.literature-positioning: Compare closely related settings, data and input assumptions; include relevant contrary and negative findings.
guidance.method-specification: Inspect split versions, preprocessing, training, tuning, architecture, inference and relevant compute choices.
guidance.design-validity: Inspect leakage, selection access, independent evaluation units and the design needed for causal or mechanism claims.
guidance.comparison-fairness: Track data, annotation access, tuning, capacity, compute, inference calls and postprocessing; label copied versus reproduced baselines.
guidance.analysis-uncertainty: State what varies across runs or samples and how uncertainty is computed; require neither a universal seed count nor a significance test.
guidance.robustness-failures: Probe claim-relevant ablations, shifts, workloads or adverse cases rather than demanding unrelated experiments.
guidance.claim-evidence-entailment: Keep benchmark performance, component mechanism, broad generalization and deployment benefit distinct.
guidance.concept-definitions: Operationalize robustness, efficiency and generalization; keep validation and test roles distinct.
guidance.notation-units: Reconcile tensor shapes, loss terms, metric direction, latency units and hardware-dependent quantities.
guidance.numbers-denominators: Identify image, scene, participant, dataset and run counts; distinguish relative changes from percentage points.
guidance.cross-section-alignment: Propagate split, model version, input access and principal result across summaries, displays and supplement.
guidance.title-abstract: Convey task, approach and principal measured finding without broadening its tested conditions.
guidance.introduction-logic: Connect the specific problem and prior limitation to the contribution using genre-appropriate previews.
guidance.paragraph-sentence-logic: Explain module, operation and comparison dependencies; preserve result qualifiers.
guidance.jargon-acronyms: Define necessary method terms for the intended ML or adjacent-field reader without deleting precise distinctions.
guidance.reader-teachback: Ask a blind reader to recover task, changed mechanism, supporting comparison and tested scope from the saved packet.
guidance.figures-tables: Inspect visual examples and quantitative encodings, including scales, input conditions, sampling units and uncertainty.
guidance.reproducibility-artifacts: Trace results to versions, configurations and commands or a restricted-access route; distinguish availability from execution.
guidance.limitations-transfer: Bound conclusions by evaluated distributions, resources and uses; untested deployment remains unresolved.
guidance.ethics-disclosures: Review actual data rights, annotation practices, sensitive uses and assistance; medical images alone do not imply a trial.
guidance.venue-compliance: Verify the actual cycle, track and stage rather than inheriting historical formatting or policies.

guidance.research-question: Define formal target, objects, regime and what proposition, separation or bound would answer the question.
guidance.motivation-gap: Explain what remains unresolved under the relevant assumptions; changing assumptions or regimes can change the gap.
guidance.contribution-calibration: Distinguish theorem, proof technique, characterization, impossibility result or sharper bound; empirical results are not required merely to score well.
guidance.literature-positioning: Compare theorem statements, assumptions, quantifiers, rates and regimes rather than only paper-level descriptions.
guidance.method-specification: Specify constructions, algorithms, definitions, proof strategy and dependencies needed to reconstruct the argument.
guidance.design-validity: Inspect proof obligations, logical steps, boundary cases and lemma assumptions; locating a theorem environment is not proof review.
guidance.comparison-fairness: Compare guarantees under compatible assumptions and regimes; explain tradeoffs when they differ instead of demanding benchmarks.
guidance.analysis-uncertainty: For probabilistic results inspect probability spaces, events and quantifiers; for deterministic results inspect bound dependence, regime and approximation meaning.
guidance.robustness-failures: Use counterexamples, tightness, degenerate cases or assumption sensitivity to locate boundaries; experiments are optional unless claimed.
guidance.claim-evidence-entailment: Retain decisive theorem assumptions and quantifiers in summaries; asymptotic complexity is not measured wall-clock speed.
guidance.concept-definitions: Check formal object identity, equivalence conventions and distinctions among related properties throughout proof and exposition.
guidance.notation-units: Prioritize domains, index ranges, dimensions, overloaded symbols and precise theorem or lemma references.
guidance.numbers-denominators: Inspect constants, factors, dimensions, rates and quantified counts. For a numeric-free proof, document inspected absence of numeric assertions instead of inventing counts.
guidance.cross-section-alignment: Reconcile informal guarantees with exact theorem statements, proof conditions and appendix versions.
guidance.title-abstract: Give an interpretable result and its decisive regime or assumptions; the abstract need not contain a full proof.
guidance.introduction-logic: Connect the open formal question to the result and useful intuition without assuming the reader knows the proof.
guidance.paragraph-sentence-logic: Explain dependencies among proof steps; intuition and formal argument should concern the same statement.
guidance.jargon-acronyms: Introduce specialized properties and constructions for the intended audience while preserving mathematical distinctions.
guidance.reader-teachback: Ask a blind reader to restate target, guarantee, assumptions and proof idea at the level supported by the packet.
guidance.figures-tables: Assess supplied diagrams or bound tables; N/A requires both no displays and no claim needing one, not merely a theory contribution.
guidance.reproducibility-artifacts: Complete proofs, derivation locations and dependency or formalization versions can provide reconstruction; code is not required for a noncomputational proof.
guidance.limitations-transfer: Explain excluded regimes, assumption strength and departures of practical implementations from the proved construction.
guidance.ethics-disclosures: Assess actual funding, interests, authorship, assistance and relevant applications; do not invent participant requirements.
guidance.venue-compliance: Check proof and supplement placement, length and declaration rules for the actual venue and stage.

guidance.research-question: Identify actual trial, observational, diagnostic or prediction question, population, setting and endpoint; not every health study tests treatment benefit.
guidance.motivation-gap: Explain the clinical or methodological need in care context using relevant evidence, uncertainty and alternatives.
guidance.contribution-calibration: Distinguish clinical benefit, diagnostic accuracy, prediction performance and technical feasibility; statistical novelty is not demonstrated patient benefit.
guidance.literature-positioning: Compare relevant populations, care pathways, endpoints and designs without merging incompatible clinical questions.
guidance.method-specification: Report actual eligibility, recruitment, intervention or index test, reference standard, outcomes, follow-up and missing-data handling as applicable.
guidance.design-validity: Inspect design-specific selection, confounding, allocation, masking, reference-standard or participant-overlap risks; causal inference needs justified identification assumptions.
guidance.comparison-fairness: Use the relevant clinical comparator; assess thresholds, reader access, treatment allocation or adjustment as appropriate to the design.
guidance.analysis-uncertainty: Identify estimands, analysis populations, clustering, missingness, multiplicity and precision where relevant; distinguish statistical from clinical importance.
guidance.robustness-failures: Inspect relevant sensitivity analyses, subgroup precision, harms and site or temporal variation; avoid unsupported subgroup conclusions.
guidance.claim-evidence-entailment: Do not infer utility from discrimination alone, benefit from an unsupported surrogate, or equivalence from nonsignificance.
guidance.concept-definitions: Keep disease definitions, endpoints, index tests, horizons, calibration, discrimination and clinical utility distinct.
guidance.notation-units: Check laboratory or dosage units, time horizons, risk scales and effect-measure definitions for the actual study.
guidance.numbers-denominators: Reconcile participant flow, exclusions, missing observations, events and follow-up; distinguish patients from lesions, visits or images.
guidance.cross-section-alignment: Compare endpoint, analysis population, effect and design qualifiers across abstract, body, displays and supplied protocol.
guidance.title-abstract: Use journal and design-appropriate structure; report interpretable estimates with essential population and uncertainty information.
guidance.introduction-logic: Move from the care or scientific problem to the objective, respecting journal conventions about result previews.
guidance.paragraph-sentence-logic: Keep actors, temporal order, effect measures and causal status explicit when simplifying prose.
guidance.jargon-acronyms: Explain clinical and ML terminology for the declared audience without erasing diagnostic or prognostic distinctions.
guidance.reader-teachback: Ask a blind reader to recover design, population, endpoint, result and what it establishes about care.
guidance.figures-tables: Inspect applicable flow, baseline, outcome and diagnostic displays; clarify populations, events, intervals and scales.
guidance.reproducibility-artifacts: Trace results to supplied protocol, analysis plan, data dictionary or controlled access; privacy restrictions alone do not imply failure.
guidance.limitations-transfer: Explain design limits, patient and setting applicability, residual confounding or validation gaps as relevant; untested transfer is not observed failure.
guidance.ethics-disclosures: Verify actual approval or exemption, consent, applicable registration, funding and interests against records; medical vocabulary alone does not trigger requirements.
guidance.venue-compliance: Route actual design to relevant CONSORT, STROBE, STARD, TRIPOD or other guidance and extensions; separately verify current journal rules.

guidance.research-question: Define the synthesis question and eligibility framework, including relevant populations or objects, exposures, interventions, outcomes and designs.
guidance.motivation-gap: Explain what the synthesis resolves beyond existing reviews, including changed scope or evidence rather than age alone.
guidance.contribution-calibration: Distinguish mapping, qualitative synthesis and quantitative meta-analysis; do not require inappropriate pooling.
guidance.literature-positioning: Separate prior-review context from the included-study evidence set; inspect source claims and conflicting evidence.
guidance.method-specification: Specify actual information sources, dates, complete searches, eligibility, screening, extraction, appraisal and synthesis procedures.
guidance.design-validity: Inspect search and selection coverage, duplicate handling, risk-of-bias appraisal and synthesis compatibility; checklist completion alone is not validity.
guidance.comparison-fairness: Check comparability of populations, designs, outcomes and follow-up; distinguish direct and indirect comparisons and avoid unsupported cross-study rankings.
guidance.analysis-uncertainty: For meta-analysis inspect effect harmonization, dependence, model assumptions, heterogeneity and precision; for qualitative synthesis inspect how uncertainty and conflict shape reasoning.
guidance.robustness-failures: Inspect relevant sensitivity to eligibility, appraisal, synthesis choices and missing evidence; do not mandate uninformative statistical bias tests.
guidance.claim-evidence-entailment: Tie conclusions to included evidence and its certainty; pooling associations does not itself identify causation.
guidance.concept-definitions: Distinguish records, reports, studies and participants; define harmonized outcomes and any certainty terminology used.
guidance.notation-units: Check effect directions, conversions, follow-up scales and synthesis notation; do not merge unlike quantities under one label.
guidance.numbers-denominators: Reconcile retrieval, deduplication, screening, exclusion and inclusion counts; distinguish reports, studies and per-outcome denominators.
guidance.cross-section-alignment: Reconcile search dates, eligibility, included counts, outcome sets and conclusions across abstract, flow, tables and supplement.
guidance.title-abstract: Identify synthesis type and scope, actual sources or dates, principal findings and decisive evidence limits within the required format.
guidance.introduction-logic: Connect the decision or knowledge need to what prior reviews leave unresolved and this review's objective.
guidance.paragraph-sentence-logic: Organize around the synthesis question; distinguish individual-study observations from review-level inference.
guidance.jargon-acronyms: Explain synthesis and appraisal terms; use certainty labels only with a defined assessment method.
guidance.reader-teachback: Ask a blind reader to recover eligibility scope, synthesis process, main finding and evidence limitations.
guidance.figures-tables: Inspect flow and evidence-summary displays; verify study identity, effect direction, uncertainty and duplicate counting.
guidance.reproducibility-artifacts: Trace searches, screening decisions, extraction, appraisal and synthesis code or reasoning; identify protocol deviations and access restrictions.
guidance.limitations-transfer: Distinguish review-process limits from included-study limits and explain both sets of consequences for conclusions and applicability.
guidance.ethics-disclosures: Verify funding, interests, reviewer contributions and assistance; participant requirements apply only when the actual work triggers them.
guidance.venue-compliance: Check actual journal and appropriate PRISMA guidance or extensions; selecting this profile does not make narrative related work systematic.
